videos.script: Imagine you cannot see the code at all. You have the rule, and a command that takes four words and prints a price. {{outside}} That is black-box testing. You test the system by what it does, and compare it with what it should do. {{compare}} First, take the rule one sentence at a time. Each sentence draws a line, and you test both sides of it. Sixteen fifty-nine, and seventeen hundred. Eleven years old, and twelve. {{lines}} Six cases, six passes. {{pass}} Then ask what the rule never mentions. A student, on a Wednesday. {{combination}} The program charges a quarter of the price. Is that a defect? No test can say. Only the product owner can. {{question}} Finally, feed it what nobody expected. A word for an age. A day with a capital letter. A time that does not exist. {{nonsense}} Some inputs make it crash. Worse, some make it quietly charge the wrong price. {{end}}
